source.author: verg
source.text: Transiit et parmam mucro, levia arma minacis, et tunicam, molli mater quam neverat auro, implevitque sinum sanguis; tum vita per auras concessit maesta ad manis corpusque reliquit.
source.text_original: Transiit et parmam mucro, levia arma minacis, / et tunicam, molli mater quam neverat auro, / implevitque sinum sanguis; tum vita per auras / concessit maesta ad manis corpusque reliquit.
source.text_english: The sword-point passed through his shield as well, the light arms of the threatening man, and the tunic, which his mother had woven with soft gold, and blood filled his bosom; then, life, grieving, withdrew through the air to the shades below and left the body.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: uariam habuit et Ioseph tunicam, quam ei texuit mater ecclesia.
reuse.text_original: uariam habuit et Ioseph tunicam, quam ei texuit mater ecclesia.
reuse.text_english: Joseph had a coat of many colors, which mother Church wove for him.
